content.title: About
content.content: The beech mushroom (Boletus edulis) is an edible fungus that grows in coniferous and mixed forests, often near beech trees. It has a large brown cap, a thick fleshy stalk, and a delicate nutty aroma. It is considered a delicacy in many culinary traditions.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The beech mushroom is often called the “king of forest mushrooms” because of its size and flavor.
It forms a mycorrhizal relationship with beech roots, enhancing the tree’s water and nutrient uptake.
In some regions the collection of beech mushrooms is regulated to protect wild populations.
Dried beech mushrooms can be stored for up to a year while retaining aroma and nutrients.
In Japan, beech mushrooms are frequently used in dashi broth and sushi.

items.title: Rich in protein
items.content: Beech mushrooms provide about 3 g of protein per 100 g, making them a good source of plant‑based protein.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: They contain less than 1 g of fat per 100 g, mostly polyunsaturated.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: They are a source of niacin, riboflavin and vitamin B12, supporting energy metabolism.

items.title: Minerals
items.content: Beech mushrooms supply potassium, phosphorus, selenium and copper, important for heart and immune health.

items.title: Antioxidants
items.content: Ergothioneine and polyphenols in the mushrooms help protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Allergic reactions
items.content: Some individuals may experience skin rashes or gastrointestinal symptoms after consuming mushrooms.

items.title: Toxicity from misidentification
items.content: Several poisonous species resemble beech mushrooms, so inexperienced foragers should be cautious.

items.title: Purine content
items.content: Raw mushrooms contain modest amounts of purines, which can aggravate gout if eaten in excess.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Beech mushrooms can be sautéed, stewed, baked, or added to soups and sauces. Before cooking, trim the fibrous skin from the stalk and slice the caps into sizable pieces. Dried mushrooms should be re‑hydrated in water for 20–30 minutes before using them as fresh.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Fresh beech mushrooms keep in the refrigerator in a paper bag for 3–5 days. For long‑term storage, dry them in a shaded area or a dehydrator, then store in an airtight container in a cool, dry place.
